Job Description: 2027 Technology Graduate Programme - AI-Native Data Platform Engineering TD Securities are offering an exceptional opportunity to join a diverse and dynamic team through our 12-month Technology Internship on the AI-Native Data Platform Engineering team. From your first day on the TDS Graduate Programme, you will contribute as part of a global team at one of the world’s largest banking institutions. Our development programme offers structured training, exposure to meaningful projects, and opportunities to build the knowledge and skills needed for a career in financial markets. You will gain practical experience on projects that support the team and develop a foundation for your future career within a global organisation. Internship Overview Contract Type: Full-time, 12-Month Graduate Programme Dates: July 2027 Location: Dublin Office : 1 Molesworth Street Candidates must have an unrestricted right to work in Ireland throughout the entire duration of the internship. Team Overview: The TDS Data Platform Engineering team is building the next generation of data platforms where data products, AI agents, and self-service analytics work together to help users discover, understand, and consume data more effectively. Our mission is to provide a scalable, secure, and AI-ready data platform that empowers domain teams to build and own data products while enabling consumers to interact with data through modern experiences such as AI agents, natural language interfaces, and intelligent automation. As a Graduate Analyst or a 6-month Intern, you will help shape how AI and data platforms converge. You will work on technologies such as Large Language Models (LLMs), Agentic AI, Model Context Protocol (MCP), data products, APIs, cloud-native platforms, and analytics solutions. You will collaborate with domain owners, data engineers, application teams, and platform engineers to create innovative solutions that make data easier to discover, understand, and use. We are a highly collaborative team that values curiosity, experimentation, continuous learning, and delivering business value through simple, scalable, and user-centric solutions. How you will Contribute: Help design and build AI-ready data platform capabilities that enable self-service data discovery and usage. Develop AI agents and MCP-based integrations that allow users to interact with data products using natural language. Collaborate with domain owners to understand their data products and create intelligent experiences that simplify data consumption. Build APIs, services, and automation frameworks that expose data and business capabilities to AI agents and applications. Contribute to the development of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) solutions using enterprise data sources. Assist in building and maintaining scalable data pipelines and cloud-native data services. Create proof-of-concepts exploring emerging technologies in AI, data engineering, and developer productivity. Partner with platform users to understand pain points and improve platform usability and adoption. Develop tools that help users discover datasets, understand lineage, definitions, ownership, and usage patterns. Support the implementation of governance, security, and access controls for AI-enabled solutions. Participate in platform monitoring, troubleshooting, testing, and continuous improvement activities. Contribute to technical documentation, architecture reviews, and knowledge-sharing initiatives. Apply engineering best practices including clean code, automated testing, CI/CD, and secure software development. Continuously research emerging AI and data technologies and evaluate their relevance to the platform. Key Technologies: The successful graduate will gain experience in: AI Agents, Agentic Workflows, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) Large Language Models (LLMs), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and Prompt Engineering Java (Spring Boot) for APIs and backend services Python for data engineering, automation, analytics, and AI solutions Apache Spark and Dremio for large-scale data processing and data products Azure Data Platform Ecosystem including Databricks, AKS, ADLS, ADF, and Azure AI Services Vector Databases and Semantic Search technologies REST APIs, gRPC, and Event-Driven Architectures Kafka for real-time data movement GitHub, GitHub Actions, Jira, and Confluence Observability platforms such as Dynatrace and Datadog Security, Governance, and Data Catalog technologies Who we are looking for: Recent graduate (2026) or upcoming 2027 graduate with a Bachelors or Masters degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, or a related field. Passion for solving business problems using data and AI. Strong curiosity and willingness to explore emerging technologies. Excellent communication and collaboration skills. Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment with a bias toward learning and experimentation. Interest in understanding both technology and business domains. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills. Programming experience in one or more languages such as Java, Python, JavaScript, or C#. Understanding of APIs and modern software development principles. Basic SQL and data modelling knowledge. Familiarity with Git and collaborative software development practices. Interest in AI, machine learning, large language models, or intelligent systems. Previous experience with the below considered an asset: Experience with Generative AI, LLMs, RAG, AI Agents, or MCP. Knowledge of data engineering concepts and distributed data processing. Exposure to cloud platforms such as Azure, AWS, or GCP.o   Familiarity with Databricks, Spark, Dremio, or similar analytics platforms. Understanding of vector databases and semantic search concepts. Experience building APIs using Spring Boot, FastAPI, or similar frameworks.o   Knowledge of containerization technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes. Passion for creating intuitive user experiences and self-service platforms. Interest in Data Mesh, data products, data governance, and AI-enabled analytics. How to Apply: All applicants are required to submit their CV and a Cover Letter. Only complete applications will be accepted. Please note that your application will not be considered complete without submitting your CV and Cover Letter. If during the application process your Cover Letter or CV was not uploaded, please send an email to dublinrecruitment@tdescurities.com titled “2027 Technology Grad - Your First & Last Name”. Corporate Profile - TD Bank Group: Headquartered in Toronto, Canada, with more than 85,000 employees in offices around the world, The Toronto-Dominion Bank and its subsidiaries are collectively known as TD Bank Group (TD). TD offers a full range of financial products and services more than 25 million customers worldwide through three key business lines: Canadian Retail including TD Canada Trust, Business Banking, TD Auto Finance (Canada), TD Wealth (Canada), TD Direct Investing and TD Insurance U.S. Retail including TD Bank, America’s Most Convenient Bank, TD Auto Finance (U.S.), TD Wealth (U.S.) and TD’s investment in TD Ameritrade Wholesale Banking including TD Securities TD Securities is a leading global corporate and investment bank, delivering capital markets products, advisory services, trading expertise and market insights to corporate, government and institutional clients worldwide. Operating in 30 cities across the globe, we combine deep industry knowledge, innovation and global connectivity to help clients achieve their ambitions. Through our offices in London, Dublin and Belfast, we support clients across the UK, Ireland and Europe while leveraging the strength of our global platform and expertise. We are growth-oriented, people-focused, and community-minded. As a team, we work to deliver value for our clients every day. Inclusiveness At TD, we are committed to fostering an inclusive, accessible environment, where all employees and customers feel valued, respected and supported. We are dedicated to building a workforce that reflects the diversity of our customers and communities in which we live and serve. If you require an accommodation for the recruitment/interview process (including alternate formats of materials, or accessible meeting rooms or other accommodation), please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs. Every day, we strive to make every interaction, product, and experience remarkably human and refreshingly simple for over 27 million households and businesses in Canada, the United States and around the world. More than 95,000 TD colleagues bring their skills, talent, and creativity to foster deeper relationships, ensure disciplined execution, and build a simpler, faster banking experience. TD is deeply committed to being a leader in client experience, that is why we believe that all colleagues, no matter where they work, are client facing. c06de04bd1a22d6544ed.description: Data governance is geen papierwerk. Het is wat bepaalt of organisaties kunnen sturen, opschalen en verantwoorden.  Bij adesso helpen we organisaties datagedreven werken  duurzaam  te organiseren. Niet door alleen modellen en policies te introduceren, maar door governance te verbinden aan  businesswaarde, adoptie en besluitvorming .  Voor ons Data & AI-team zoeken we een  Data Governance Consultant  die structuur aanbrengt, eigenaarschap afdwingt en management meeneemt in volwassen datagebruik.     Jouw rol   Jij brengt orde in complexiteit.  Als Data Governance Consultant ben jij de drijvende kracht achter het professionaliseren van data governance binnen complexe organisaties. Je verbindt strategie, operatie en technologie tot één werkend geheel — en zorgt dat data geen risico is, maar een versneller.  Je opereert als trusted advisor voor C-level, management, business, architecten en datateams. Waar eigenaarschap ontbreekt, organiseer jij het. Waar besluitvorming stokt, breng jij helderheid. Waar governance versnipperd is, bouw jij samenhang.  Dit is geen rol waarin je “een framework uitrolt”. Je  bouwt een operating model dat blijft werken .     Wat je doet (in de praktijk)      Strategie & operating model     Ontwerpen en implementeren van data governance strategieën en operating models (o.a. DAMA-DMBOK).    Vertalen van businessdoelen naar governanceprincipes, rollen, policies en werkprocessen.    Uitvoeren van data maturity assessments en volwassenheidsscans.    Vertalen van business use cases naar data-initiatieven en concrete roadmaps.    Adviseren van management en directie over governance, risico’s en prioriteiten.     Governance & stewardship     Opzetten en activeren van data stewardship (top-down én bottom-up).    Inrichten van besluitvorming rondom definities, standaarden, business rules en datakwaliteit.    Organiseren van steering, ownership en governance-structuren die gedragen worden.     Data quality, metadata & lineage     Werken met datamodellering (basisniveau), data lineage en impactanalyses.    Inrichten en verbeteren van datakwaliteit- en datamanagementprocessen.    Ondersteunen van data product teams bij datacontracten en lifecycle management.     Alignment & change     Faciliteren van workshops en werksessies op verschillende organisatieniveaus.    Actief stakeholdermanagement in complexe en soms politieke omgevingen.    Overbruggen van business en IT — inclusief het oplossen van spanningen en escalaties.    Vergroten van data literacy, eigenaarschap en bewustzijn door de hele organisatie.    Richting, focus en tempo brengen in governance- en verandertrajecten.          Wat jij meebrengt   Je bent inhoudelijk sterk én organisatiesensitief.    Minimaal 5 jaar ervaring in data governance, data management of dataconsultancy.     Aantoonbare ervaring met:     Data governance & operating models    Data kwaliteit en data lineage    Data stewardship    Basis data-architectuur      CDMP-certificering (of vergelijkbaar).    Erva

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic is growing quickly across EMEA, and we need recruiters who can help us hire exceptional people into the teams that bring our work to customers. We’re looking for a Recruiter, GTM to join our Talent team in Dublin and own full-cycle recruiting across our Go-To-Market organization, with a particular focus on Applied AI.

This is a full-cycle individual-contributor role. You’ll partner with Applied AI and GTM leaders to define what great looks like, build pipelines in markets where these roles are still new, and close candidates who have competing offers. Some of the roles you’ll run won’t have an established market benchmark, so you’ll help build the playbook as well as follow it. Priorities shift quickly, and you’ll have real ownership of the searches you run.

Key responsibilities

  • Own full-cycle recruiting for Applied AI and broader GTM roles across EMEA, with a focus on London, Paris and Munich, from intake through offer and close
  • Run intake sessions that scope the role, calibrate the bar, and challenge hiring managers where expectations don’t match the market
  • Screen candidates against the JD with enough technical judgment to separate strong from merely well-presented
  • Source and engage active and passive candidates, building diverse and competitive pipelines in markets where talent is scarce
  • Run structured, rigorous and candidate-centric interview processes that uphold Anthropic’s hiring bar
  • Work with the broader Talent team, People Partners and Compensation to structure offers and guide candidates to close
  • Own pipeline health, tracking conversion, calibration and time-in-stage, and use the data to give hiring managers clear recommendations
  • Help build and document the Applied AI and GTM hiring playbooks as the team scales

Minimum qualifications

  • 4+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience, with a track record of closing strong candidates in competitive markets
  • Demonstrated experience recruiting GTM or customer-facing roles in the UK and European markets, with working knowledge of local talent dynamics, compensation norms and employment practices
  • Strong stakeholder partnership: you build trust quickly with senior hiring managers in fast-moving environments
  • Willingness and ability to build technical depth quickly enough to run credible intake sessions and screens for Applied AI roles
  • Proven ability to maintain quality under volume pressure and manage multiple searches at once
  • Comfort with ambiguity and with building something new rather than running an established playbook
  • Self-starter who works autonomously while staying aligned with global hiring strategy

When a transformer slips three weeks at the factory, a data hall slips three weeks at the site. We're hiring a Supply Chain Delivery Manager to own that equipment from purchase order to dock. You will be the site-facing supply chain lead for a regional portfolio of data center projects: tracking every OFE line item against the construction schedule, running factory and logistics escalations with OEMs, holding suppliers and general contractors accountable for delivery performance, and giving leadership a clear, converged picture of delivery risk across the portfolio. Your job is to make sure equipment production and delivery are never the reason a site misses its ready-for-service date. This is a senior individual-contributor role on the Compute DC Infrastructure team, working daily with Construction, Electrical and Mechanical Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, Commissioning, and our general contractors and OEMs. It is not a category-management or negotiation role — Sourcing owns supplier strategy and commercial terms — and it is not a people-management role. The emphasis is execution: schedules, escalations, logistics, and site readiness. What You'll Do Delivery planning and schedule integration Own the end-to-end OFE delivery plan for each site in your portfolio: order placement, engineering submittal/approval milestones, production slots, FAT dates, ship dates, and required-on-site (ROS) dates, integrated with the GC's construction schedule. Engage during preconstruction with Construction, Engineering, and the GC to set OFE delivery expectations, sequence equipment arrivals to the build, and identify schedule risk before POs are cut. Lead OFE kickoff meetings at the site level with the GC and internal construction teams, establishing points of contact, delivery windows, receiving requirements, and escalation paths. Maintain the single source of truth for OFE status across the portfolio — a live tracker of every line item, its milestone dates, and its risk rating. Manage laydown, staging, and interim storage decisions when site readiness and equipment arrival diverge; coordinate with Quality and Commissioning on receiving inspection and storage/preservation requirements. Ensure equipment arrives complete — accessories, spares, documentation, and vendor startup support scheduled — so installation and commissioning are not delayed by missing pieces. Risk management and reporting Identify, triage, and report delivery risks across the portfolio; propose solutions and drive decisions to protect capacity milestones. Establish and lead recurring Capacity Delivery Reviews giving leadership converged visibility into OFE delivery status and risk by site and by equipment category. Track delivery KPIs — on-time-to-ROS, schedule drift by supplier and category, escalation cycle time, expedite spend — and use them to surface systemic issues. Feed lessons learned back into Sourcing (lead-time assumptions, contract delivery terms, buffer strategy) and Construction (ROS sequencing) to improve the next program. Strong written and verbal communication — you can turn a messy delivery problem into a one-page recommendation for leadership. Data-fluent: you build and maintain trackers and dashboards, and you'd rather look at the numbers than trust a status email. Thrive with high autonomy in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment; you own outcomes, not just updates. Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field, or equivalent experience. About the Role

Anthropic's infrastructure fleet spans a growing set of clouds, neoclouds, and on-prem sites.  Every part of it is expanding rapidly. Capacity Engineering is the team that connects every stage of that growth, from capacity planning to supply management to capacity delivery to utilization. We partner on supply deals, wire telemetry from day zero, own the canonical capacity data layer, and build the planning and enforcement tools every research and product team relies on.

As an Infrastructure Capacity Planner on the Demand Planning team, you'll own the medium-range demand forecast for every resource class we consume: accelerators, CPU, storage, network, and managed services. Your forecast will support sourcing and purchasing, prioritization, efficiency targets, and workload optimization.

Key responsibilities

  • Build and own the medium-range multi-resource demand forecast: accelerators by chip/interconnect class, CPU by shape, storage by tier and access pattern, egress by path, managed services by SKU — driven by model roadmap, RL/inference growth, eval volume, and retention policy rather than trend lines.
  • Run the plan-vs-reality loop. Diff planned allocations against observed fleet occupancy weekly, surface unrecorded trades and stale allocations, and drive variance toward zero with our planning-tools and data teams.
  • Qualify each incoming capacity tranche against the forecast before signature: right shape, region, quarter, and supporting-resource envelope (storage, egress, CPU). 
  • Partner with Finance and cost-efficiency teams to turn the forecast into core drivers covering the large majority (≥80%) of non-accelerator spend, and to aim savings work where waste will appear next.

What you bring

  • Have done capacity, demand, or supply planning for large-scale technical infrastructure (cloud, HPC, hyperscale, or a large internal platform) and can articulate the difference between a forecast, a plan, and an allocation.
  • Build the model yourself rather than specifying it for someone else: SQL against a warehouse, Python/pandas or a proper forecasting/optimization stack.
  • Understand data-center resource classes well to know why storage and egress don't forecast like GPUs, and why a contract's headline chip count is rarely the binding constraint.
  • Prefer simple, inspectable models to clever opaque ones, and instrument your own forecast error.

Preferred qualifications

  • Direct experience with cloud or neocloud providers on reserved-capacity onboarding, private offers, or capacity commitments.
  • Demand planning or forecasting experience for accelerator fleets, including translating research or product roadmaps into resource requirements.
  • Data center or colocation delivery experience: power and space planning, network turn-up, site acceptance criteria, and vendor management.
  • Experience with accelerator health and burn-in, collective-communications sanity testing, or fleet-health SLOs, and the ability to define healthy rigorously.
  • Experience building lifecycle or state-machine services, or systems of record for infrastructure assets.
  • Experience onboarding a new hardware generation into an existing scheduler and observability stack.

About the Role Anthropic manages one of the industry's largest AI fleets — spanning multiple accelerator families, cpu families and clouds. The Capacity Engineering team is responsible for making sure all our infrastructure resources are accounted for, well-utilized, and efficiently allocated. We own the data, tooling, and operational systems that let Anthropic plan, measure, and maximize utilization across first-party and third-party compute. As an engineer on Capacity Engineering, you will build the production systems that power this work: data pipelines that ingest and normalize telemetry from heterogeneous cloud environments, observability tooling that gives the org real-time visibility into fleet health, and performance instrumentation that measures how efficiently every major workload uses the hardware it’s running on. You will be expected to write production-quality code every day, operate alongside Kubernetes-native infrastructure at meaningful scale, and directly influence decisions around Capacity. You’ll collaborate closely with research engineering, infrastructure, inference, and finance teams. The work requires someone who can move between data engineering, systems engineering, and observability with comfort — and who thrives in a high-autonomy, high-ambiguity environment. This is a pipeline role feeding four areas. Depending on your background and business priority, you’ll focus primarily in one, but the boundaries are fluid and the problems overlap: Data platform Pipelines that ingest occupancy and utilization telemetry from Kubernetes clusters, normalize billing and usage across cloud providers, and serve the BigQuery tables the rest of the org queries against. Correctness, completeness, and latency are the job, not a footnote. Consumers range from research engineers to finance to leadership, so it's product work as much as engineering: defining schema contracts, making data discoverable, and figuring out what people actually need. Planning Knowing what the fleet has, where it's going, and what's in the way. Making the state of the fleet legible and actionable in real time: cluster health tooling, capacity planning platforms, alerting on occupancy drops and allocation problems, and systemic fixes to scheduling and fragmentation. Kubernetes operations on one side, cross-team coordination on the other. Efficiency Measuring and improving how effectively every major workload uses the hardware it runs on. Instrumenting utilization across training, inference, and eval systems, building benchmarking infrastructure, establishing per-config baselines, and working directly with system-owning teams to close the gaps. The metric has to be good enough that the team on the hook for it agrees with the number. Attribution and forecasting Connecting what the fleet costs to what the business is doing with it. Reconciling CSP billing exports against vendor telemetry and internal systems with mismatched schemas, attributing spend to the workloads and teams that generate it, and turning inference demand signals and research roadmaps into a defensible compute plan. Efficiency metrics have to survive contact with finance: stripped of pure demand and unit-price effects, reproducible month over month, and legible to a CFO. Key responsibilities Build the planning and allocation stack — the tools leadership uses to allocate capacity, teams use to plan against their allocations, and the scheduler enforces. Cross-region and cross-provider placement, guardrails, queueing, occupancy KPIs. Drive the efficiency programs: stranding and rightsizing, unused capacity recovery, and job-level utilization across training, inference, and eval. Establish per-config baselines and work with system-owning teams to close the gaps. Directly influence decisions around a significant area of company investment. Own attribution and forecasting — reconcile billing across ten-plus providers against telemetry and internal systems, attribute spend to the workloads that generate it, and turn demand signals and research roadmaps into a defensible compute plan and supply pipeline. Build the data platform underneath all of it: pipelines ingesting occupancy, utilization, and cost from a rapidly diversifying fleet into BigQuery, with real ownership of completeness, latency SLOs, and gap detection. Every new provider is a net-new integration. Operate Kubernetes-native systems at scale — collection agents, workload labeling, and the taint/reservation/scheduling behavior that determines what capacity is actually usable. Treat the output as a product, not a pipeline. Gather your own requirements, define schema contracts, and design for consumers ranging from research engineers to a CFO — including on-call and SLOs, because these surfaces are load-bearing for the company. What you bring A strong track record building and operating production systems. This is a hands-on engineering role with a devops flavor. Python and SQL at production quality. Most pipeline code is Python; the presentation layer is BigQuery SQL, including table-valued functions and views. Both need to be idiomatic, well-tested, and maintainable. Deep experience with at least one major cloud provider (Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Azure) and its operations Experience with observability tooling stack, including Prometheus, PromQL, and Grafana, including writing recording rules and building monitoring that engineering teams rely on. Ability to gather your own requirements and work across organizational boundaries in an ambiguous environment with limited direction. Preferred qualifications Experience with capacity planning, resource management, or cost attribution systems at a hyperscaler or in a large-scale machine learning environment. Time spent in product engineering and developer experience absolutely counts here. Scheduling and packing efficiency experience, or profiling-driven optimization of large distributed workloads. Multi-cloud data ingestion experience, especially normalizing billing exports, reservation APIs, on-demand capacity reservations, commitments, and vendor telemetry from providers with different billing arrangements. Total cost of ownership and forecasting experience, including decomposing whether infrastructure growth is causal or correlated with business drivers. Accelerator infrastructure familiarity. GPU metrics (DCGM), TPU utilization, Trainium power and utilization metrics, or experience with machine learning training and inference systems at the hardware level. Experience building internal data products with self-service access, schema contracts, API serving, documentation, and discoverability. Not just pipelines, but thinking about how the data gets consumed. Storage efficiency, retention, and lifecycle program experience at very large scale. c5108aa51ca11ad1805e.description:
Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI. At our core is the Celonis Context Model — which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence into a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can actually understand, turning AI's operational blind spots into operational clarity. World's leading companies trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. We believe there's a massive opportunity to unlock global productivity and sustainability by giving AI the context to understand how every business process really works. Join our mission to make processes work for people, companies, and the planet.

The Role:
We are looking for a Client Value Partner, Utilities—a seasoned industry executive who can bridge the gap between energy transition strategy and operational excellence. You will act as the primary accountable lead for one of America's largest strategic energy companies, translating C-level vision into clear, realized value.

As a Client Value Partner, you are a "go-to" strategic advisor within our Energy go-to-market organization. You will move beyond standard customer success to link Celonis capabilities to key outcomes specific to Power Generation, Transmission & Distribution, and Renewable Energy assets.

You will work in partnership with the Celonis Sales Teams and have full responsibility for the end-to-end value journey of our top-tier customers. You are our customers’ trusted advisor, helping them mobilize resources, achieve their strategic goals, and realize significant value using the Celonis Process Intelligence Platform.

In collaboration with our partners, Product, and Engineering teams, you will drive measurable business impact across complex, decentralized operating environments. You will blend deep utility expertise with a proven strategy consulting skill set to spearhead data-driven transformation at the forefront of one of the fastest-growing tech companies worldwide.

The work you’ll do:

Identify & Frame Value

  • Translate Strategy to Operations: Analyze the client's strategic goals (e.g., Decarbonization, Rate Base Growth, Grid Modernization) and map them to a long-term vision utilizing the Celonis platform.
  • Target High-Impact Areas: Architect the "COO" or "CFO" agenda—optimizing end-to-end value chains such as Capital Projects (EPC), Enterprise Asset Management (EAM), Meter-to-Cash, and Supply Chain resilience.
  • Build the Business Case: Construct robust, board-level business cases that articulate the financial impact of Process Intelligence (e.g., impact on O&M efficiency, ROE improvement, or Storm Response agility) to C-Suite executives.
  • Build demos and strategic roadmaps, leveraging industry benchmarks and best practices in order to embed Celonis as a core pillar of the client's digital utility strategy.
  • Undertake Value Assessments and communicate the value opportunity and strategic roadmap to C-Level executives.

Realize Value

  • Drive Engagement Success: Lead the executive relationship and value workstream for large-scale transformations, ensuring the program effectively delivers on its "digital twin" promise across diverse operating companies.
  • Orchestrate the Ecosystem: Guide customers on organization design and the maturation of Centers of Excellence (CoE), mobilizing global cross-functional teams (Services, Product, Engineering) to ensure seamless delivery across a federated organizational structure.
  • Solve Systemic Challenges: Work cross-functionally to tackle difficult implementation hurdles, helping customers define standards for regulatory reporting (FERC/NERC), work order management, and enterprise-wide change initiatives.
  • Facilitate business value workshops and use Celonis to identify and qualify opportunities for process enhancement in Operations, Finance, and Procurement.
  • Derive improvement measures in core business functions and initiate improvement actions and enterprise-wide change initiatives.
  • Present results and realized value to senior management and C-level executives.

Scale Value

  • Codify Best Practices: Turn our client successes into reusable assets, playbooks, and thought leadership for the broader Energy & Utilities practice.
  • Mentor & Enable: Act as a senior leader for the team, coaching junior members and managers on executive relationship management, utility regulatory nuances, and team performance.
  • Product Feedback: Serve as the "Voice of the Customer" to our Product teams, ensuring our development roadmap aligns with the specific asset-intensive needs of the sector.
  • Responsible for the end-to-end customer value journey, landing, expanding, adoption and renewing.
    Build a strategic expansion roadmap for customers, embedding Celonis Process Intelligence Platform as a strategic business transformation platform in their organization.
  • Provide feedback to our product development teams to enhance the Celonis platform and Apps based on new use cases.

The qualifications you need:

  • Deep Industry Experience: 15+ years of relevant experience, ideally combining time at a top-tier Utility, Energy Conglomerate, or Renewables developer with Strategy Consulting. You understand the complexities of regulated vs. unregulated markets.
  • Domain Expertise: You possess granular knowledge of the value chain, specifically in areas such as Asset Lifecycle Management, Capital Project Controls, Supply Chain, and Customer Operations (CIS).
  • Value Realization Skills: You have a track record of driving large-scale transformation programs. You understand how to impact the P&L through capital efficiency, outage reduction, and working capital optimization.
  • Technical Fluency: You understand the modern utility stack (SAP IS-U, Maximo, Oracle Primavera) and how to translate Celonis use cases into the customer's specific business landscape.
  • Stakeholder Management: Extensive experience presenting to and influencing C-Level executives (COO, CFO, CIO). You can navigate complex holding company structures and have the power of persuasion through data, facts, and confidence.
  • Builder Mentality: You are comfortable working with ambiguity and possess an entrepreneurial leadership style that inspires teams.
  • Degree: MBA strongly preferred; Degree in Engineering, Business, Economics, or related field required.

Visa sponsorship is not offered for this role.

The base salary range below is for the role in the specified location, based on a Full Time Schedule.

Total compensation package will include base salary + bonus/commission + equity + benefits (health, dental, life, 401k, and paid time off). Please note that the base salary range is a guideline, and that the actual total compensation offer will be determined based on various factors, including, but not limited to, applicant's qualifications, skills, experiences, and location.
The base salary range below is for the role in New York, based on a Full Time Schedule.
$212,000—$270,000 USD

What Celonis can offer you:

  • Pioneer Innovation: Work with the global leader in Process Mining and the Process Intelligence Graph to shape the future of AI-driven business operations.
  • Ownership from Day 1: Every full-time "Celonaut" is an owner, receiving Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) and merit-based refresh grants.
  • Unrivaled Family Support: Benefit from our inclusive parental leave policy—24 weeks of fully paid leave for primary carers and 12 weeks for supporting carers, available from your first day of employment.
  • Work-Life Integration: Enjoy Unlimited PTO (in applicable regions) and generous PTO globally, as well as a flexible hybrid work model that balances remote focus with vibrant office collaboration.
  • Continuous Growth: Elevate your skills through our 70-20-10 learning framework, mentorship programs, and access to a dedicated learning platform.
  • Holistic Well-being: Prioritize your health with subsidized Wellhub memberships, mental health counseling, and dedicated "Wellness Weeks" that prioritize work/life balance.
  • Drive Sustainability: Participate in annual Impact Days, where you receive paid time off to volunteer for community and environmental causes with your local office, or virtually.
  • Global Inclusion & Belonging: Find community through our Inclusion Think Tank and participate in our annual Inclusion Days, ensuring every voice is heard and valued.
  • Value-Driven Impact: Join a mission-led organization where our core values—Live for Customer Value, The Best Team Wins, We Own It, and Earth Is Our Future—drive every decision.

About Us:

Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI, empowering organizations to analyze, design, and operate AI-driven processes. The Celonis Platform is powered by the Celonis Context Model, which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence to create a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can understand — turning AI’s operational blind spots into operational clarity. Industry-leading companies around the world trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. Celonis is headquartered in Munich, Germany, and New York City, USA, with more than 20 offices worldwide.

Get familiar with the Celonis Process Intelligence Platform by watching this video.

Celonis Inclusion Statement:

At Celonis, we believe our people make us who we are and that “The Best Team Wins”. We know that the best teams are made up of people who bring different perspectives to the table. And when everyone feels included, able to speak up and knows their voice is heard - that's when creativity and innovation happen.

Your Privacy:

Any information you submit to Celonis as part of your application will be processed in accordance with Celonis’ Accessibility and Candidate Notices

By submitting this application, you confirm that you agree to the storing and processing of your personal data by Celonis as described in our Privacy Notice for the Application and Hiring Process.

Use of Artificial Intelligence Tools

We rely on an artificial intelligence tool to match the information from your resume to the relevant Celonis job descriptions. This processing is limited to the information provided in your resume or in your candidate profile. The tool produces a match score per candidate for a role, suggests preliminary ranking, and provides recommendations.

The tool is only used for support in parts of the job application process, including to facilitate the identification of the relevant Celonis Jobs for candidates and recruiters. All final decisions are made by hiring managers and the Celonis talent acquisition team. Hiring managers and HR specialists use this tool responsibly, are aware of the risk of potential bias, and are equipped to mitigate it.

Please be aware of common job offer scams, impersonators and frauds. Learn more here.

About MESH  
 MESH is automating rebar fabrication and construction processes using robotics and software. Our mission is to bring modern robotics and industrial-grade automation to one of the most fragmented and under-invested industries, enabling faster, safer, and more precise construction through systems that integrate seamlessly into existing workflows. 
 We design and deploy robotic solutions that operate in harsh, real-world production environments — not labs or demos. Our work spans mechanical systems, robotics, software, and industrial automation, with a strong focus on robustness, simplicity, and deployability. 
 MESH is based in Switzerland, with in-house workshops and robot testing facilities. We work closely with partners across the construction and machinery ecosystem and regularly test our systems in production and on-site environments. We value close collaboration and hands-on engineering and primarily work on-site with our hardware.  
  About the Role  
 We are looking for highly motivated interns to join our engineering team. You'll be exposed to real-world engineering challenges from day one, working directly on features and developments that translate into our products — not side projects or simulations. Depending on your background and interests, your work can lean more mechanical, more automation/controls, or more robotics.  
 You'll work closely with our engineers in our workshop and testing facilities, seeing your designs and code go from concept to deployment on real machines operating in demanding production environments. 
 Tasks 
  What You Could Work On  
 
 Designing and iterating on mechanical components and subsystems for robotic machines 
 Building and testing electro-mechanical assemblies and fixtures 
 Developing and tuning automation/control logic (PLC, motion control, sensors, actuators) 
 Supporting robotics integration — kinematics, end-effectors, perception, or motion planning 
 Debugging and improving system robustness based on real-world testing and field data 
 Contributing to test rigs, prototypes, and documentation for our production systems 
 
 Requirements 
  What We're Looking For  
 
 Currently pursuing a degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Automation, Robotics, or a related field 
 Strong hands-on instinct — comfortable in a workshop, prototyping, and iterating quickly 
 Solid fundamentals in mechanical design (CAD), and/or controls, and/or robotics, depending on focus area 
 Practical, pragmatic problem-solving mindset — you like building things that actually work outside the lab 
 Ability to work independently while collaborating closely with a small, fast-moving team 
 Fluent in English; German is a plus 
 Available to work on-site in Switzerland 
 
  What We Offer  
 
 Ownership of features and developments that interface with out existing products 
 Hands-on experience with robotics and automation systems in real production and on-site environments

c61304c3aad5b595cfe8.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic is seeking a partnerships leader to own the tri-party motion for systems integrator partnerships selling through AWS. Global systems integrators and specialist SIs are how Claude reaches enterprise customers at scale, and AWS is the surface most of that work runs on. You will own the intersection of those two ecosystems.

In this role, you will build the go-to-market motion that turns partner interest into joint pipeline and closed revenue, working across AWS's partner organization and the AWS practices inside the world's largest integrators. You will define how Claude is positioned inside AWS partner programs, design the commercial mechanics that let partners transact and get rewarded, and build the joint plays that partners take to their customers.

This is a build role. The partner ecosystem is early, the programs are still being designed, and you will be operating across three organizations whose incentives on any given deal don’t always line up. You will help shape how frontier AI technology reaches the enterprise through the services ecosystem.

You will report directly to the Head of AWS GTM Partnerships.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute the GTM strategy for our systems integrator partnerships through AWS, including co-selling motions, joint business plans, events and segment-specific plays
  • Own forecasting, pipeline development, and revenue targets for partner-sourced and partner-influenced business
  • Design the commercial mechanics that make the partner motion work, including deal registration, marketplace program structure, and incentives
  • Build and maintain executive-level relationships across AWS's partner organization and across partner AWS practice leadership
  • Work with partners to develop repeatable, industry-specific solutions built on Claude, and help them build the delivery capability to take those solutions to market
  • Partner cross-functionally with Anthropic's alliances, sales, partner marketing, and regional cloud teams to keep the motion consistent globally while regions execute locally
  • Create and implement scalable processes for partnership operations, including escalation management, business reviews, and reporting
  • Provide strategic market intelligence and competitive insights on the partner ecosystem to inform product and commercial strategy
  • Identify where to concentrate investment across the partner portfolio and make the case to stop investing where returns are not there

Minimum qualifications

  • 12+ years of enterprise partnerships, alliances, or business development experience, with meaningful time spent on partner ecosystems
  • Proven track record of building and scaling partnerships with systems integrators, consultancies, or channel partners
  • Experience building a co-sell or channel motion from the ground up, including the commercial mechanics behind it
  • Deep understanding of how cloud and partner field organizations operate, and the incentives that drive seller and partner behavior
  • Track record of carrying and hitting a partner-sourced or partner-influenced revenue number, with credible forecasting behind it
  • Strong executive presence and demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders where you have no formal authority
  • Excellence in strategic planning, business operations, and program management
  • Ability to balance strategic thinking with tactical execution, and a willingness to concentrate effort rather than spread thin
  • Experience working with technical products and translating complex capabilities into business value
  • Ability to travel up to 25% of the time

Preferred qualifications

  • Previous experience working with AWS or another hyperscaler partner organization
  • Working knowledge of systems integrator operating models, including practice structures, delivery economics, and how services revenue drives partner decisions
  • Background in AI/ML technologies or with developer-focused platforms and their partner ecosystems
  • Experience scaling partner programs at a company moving from early traction to significant partner-driven revenue
  • Management consulting experience earlier in your career

Deadline to apply: None. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. 

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$365,000—$425,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

c99355df82284f0e933f.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the RL Teams

Our Reinforcement Learning teams play a critical role in advancing our AI systems. We've contributed to all Claude models, with significant impacts on the autonomy and coding capabilities of our latest Claude models. Our work spans several key areas:

  • Developing systems that enable models to use computers effectively

  • Advancing code generation through reinforcement learning

  • Pioneering fundamental RL research for large language models

  • Building scalable RL infrastructure and training methodologies

  • Enhancing model reasoning capabilities

We collaborate closely with Anthropic's alignment and frontier red teams to ensure our systems are both capable and safe. We partner with the applied production training team to bring research innovations into deployed models, and are dedicated to implement our research at scale. Our Reinforcement Learning teams sit at the intersection of cutting-edge research and engineering excellence, with a deep commitment to building high-quality, scalable systems that push the boundaries of what AI can accomplish.

About the Role

We're hiring for the Code RL team within the RL organization. As a Research Engineer, you'll advance our models' ability to write, edit, test, debug, and ship real software — end to end, on real codebases, with real tools — and to do it correctly, fast, and safely.

This role blends research and engineering. You'll design RL environments and coding tasks, build the reward signals and verifiers that capture what "good code" means, run training experiments on frontier models, diagnose why a model does (or doesn't) get better at a class of software-engineering work, and improve the speed and reliability of the pipelines that make all of that iterate fast. Code RL spans several focus areas — from agentic coding behaviors and code correctness, to long-horizon autonomous engineering, to high-performance code for accelerators — and we'll match you to the area where you'll have the most impact.

You may be a good fit if you:

  • Have strong software-engineering skills and deep Python expertise, including async/concurrent programming

  • Are comfortable owning systems end to end and debugging across the stack

  • Can balance research exploration with engineering implementation, and engage rigorously in shaping experimental design and interpreting results

  • Care about code quality, testing, and performance

  • Are passionate about the potential impact of AI and are committed to developing safe and beneficial systems

Strong candidates may also have:

  • Experience with reinforcement learning, RLHF, post-training, or LLM finetuning

  • Built coding agents, code-execution sandboxes, eval harnesses, verifiers, or developer tooling

  • Background in program analysis, testing, verification, compilers, or formal methods

  • Experience with PyTorch and large-scale distributed training; performance profiling and optimization of ML systems

  • CUDA / GPU or TPU kernel experience and accelerator-performance intuition

  • Experience with virtualization and sandboxed code execution environments

Related roles

If your background leans toward one of these areas specifically, you may also want to look at these postings:

  • Research Engineer, Performance RL (Reinforcement Learning) — teaching Claude to write correct, fast code for accelerators

  • Research Engineer, Universes — long-horizon, ultra-realistic agentic training environments

  • Research Engineer, Cybersecurity RL (Reinforcement Learning) — RL for security-relevant coding capabilities

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$500,000—$850,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Governments do some of the most consequential work there is: deciding benefits claims, getting veterans to care, investigating financial misconduct, running unemployment insurance, and producing the analysis that world leaders act on. Anthropic's public sector team exists to put Claude in the production path of that work. In the US and some allied governments, Claude is already in daily use across major agencies and US states.

The next steps need a particular kind of product manager: someone who can walk into an institution they have never worked with, sit with the people doing the work and find, alongside them, the workflow that matters. The best government products we know of started as an idea that came out of the room rather than a requirements document. 

The scope is large: a product portfolio here is a set of governments rather than a feature area. A year in, success looks like agencies delivering services more effectively because public servants are doing core parts of their job with Claude in the loop, and at least one thing that you learn from them shipping to every Anthropic enterprise. That is a lot of surface; you will have to choose where to go deep, and we will back the choice.

We are hiring across civilian, state and local, govtech, and national security portfolios and will match you to one on background and interest. Some portfolios require eligibility for a US security clearance, though most do not. You would be among the first product managers on the team, working with a dedicated engineering and research team and with the policy, go-to-market, customer success, and applied AI leads who already spend their days inside these agencies.

In this role, you will:

  • Alongside GTM, run discovery inside government institutions to find where Claude belongs in the production path of their work, then shape the product around what you find
  • Own product decisions for our government models and product offerings and the agency workflows built on top of them
  • Spot the government needs worth generalizing and carry them into Anthropic's broader roadmap. Many of Anthropic’s commercial features started as public-sector customer problems
  • Help Anthropic navigate government compliance regimes 
  • Partner with our cloud and integration partners 

You may be a good fit if you:

  • Have shipped successful products end-to-end. We weigh product judgment above any domain credential
  • Can point to something you built that was your idea: it came from watching people work rather than from a requirements document
  • Get things done through teams that don't report to you. In addition to the dedicated team, this role runs through a variety of partner teams inside Anthropic and many offices inside each agency.
  • Move on your own clock. You have shipped in an organization with a fast cadence, or you set the pace in an environment that didn't
  • Have built domain intuition fast in large enterprises that do not resemble each other
  • Are a US person. We have agreements with the US Government that mandate this for these roles.

Strong candidates may also have:

  • Roughly 7+ years building and shipping products, or equivalent scope
  • Real intuition for how government operates, earned either from the inside or at a digital services organization or by building products public servants actually use
  • Taken a public-sector or field requirement into a commercial product that succeeded
  • Fluency with AI products: evaluations, model behavior as part of the product surface
  • Shipped inside a FedRAMP, classified, or comparable compliance boundary
  • Negotiated with or steered large partners such as cloud providers or systems integrators
  • An active TS/SCI security clearance with the US government (relevant for only some roles)
  • Ability to travel up to 25% of the time 

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$305,000—$385,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. cd5522d0746afad1c1dc.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

We're seeking an experienced Policy Communications Manager to help drive external communications for our security, governance, and responsible scaling programs, and associated work. This role offers the opportunity to help shape how Anthropic communicates about our approach to developing secure AI systems and products, our work to uphold and iterate on our Responsible Scaling Policy framework, and the unique corporate structure that keeps the company accountable to its mission, including our Long-Term Benefit Trust (LTBT) and our status as a public benefit corporation.

You'll partner closely with our security, product, legal, governance, and Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP) teams to communicate Anthropic's approach to building safe and secure AI models as the technology becomes increasingly capable across critical domains like cybersecurity. You'll also help lead communications about how Anthropic is governed: the role of the LTBT's independent trustees in overseeing the company and electing members of our board, the obligations that come with our public benefit corporation charter, and why we believe this structure matters as AI systems grow more powerful. As governments establish regulatory frameworks for frontier AI, you'll help articulate how Anthropic approaches its transparency obligations and public reporting commitments, translating evolving requirements into clear, credible external communications. This will include balancing proactive storytelling about product security updates and launches with thoughtful handling of reactive matters as they arise. We're charting new terrain communicating about fast-moving frontier model capabilities and threat surfaces, and about institutional structures few other companies have built. You'll bring strong communications fundamentals to the role but recognize that traditional approaches may not map cleanly to the novel issues we're tackling.

The ideal candidate is an experienced issues handler with strong executive management skills, attention to detail, and the judgment to navigate sensitive topics with care. You should be able to move quickly under pressure and tight deadlines, write crisply, and distill complex security, governance, and technical topics for a broad audience while maintaining accuracy. This is a unique opportunity to help define how one of the world's leading AI safety companies communicates about the security and governance challenges that will shape the future of the technology.

Key responsibilities

  • Develop and execute communications strategies for Anthropic's approach to AI security, governance, and responsible scaling
  • Drive external communications about Anthropic's corporate governance, including the Long-Term Benefit Trust and our public benefit corporation status, explaining how these structures provide independent oversight and accountability to our mission
  • Serve as a trusted communications partner to security, product, legal, governance, and RSP leaders on sensitive, fast-moving matters
  • Develop proactive communications around emerging regulatory frameworks and transparency obligations, including public reporting commitments, disclosure requirements, and Anthropic's engagement with oversight bodies
  • Manage reactive inbound media requests on complex security and governance topics
  • Build and maintain relationships with journalists and influencers covering security, corporate governance, and technology policy
  • Prepare executives for media interviews, speaking engagements, and public appearances, developing thought leadership opportunities that position Anthropic's leaders as credible voices on AI security, governance, and responsible development
  • Write blog posts, statements, talking points, and other communications materials that explain our security, governance, and responsible scaling work clearly and accessibly, maintaining accuracy
  • Support reactive communications efforts with speed, accuracy, and sound judgment

Minimum qualifications

  • Experience in policy communications, including managing communications around complex security or governance topics
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to distill complex technical topics accurately for broad audiences
  • Experience in issues management and developing reactive communications under pressure and tight timelines
  • Strong executive management skills and a proven ability to work seamlessly across technical and non-technical teams
  • A track record of building media relationships
  • A results-oriented, high-agency working style, with a bias toward flexibility and impact
  • Comfort operating in new terrain, where the technology is evolving quickly and the right communications approach may not yet exist
  • A deep commitment to ensuring that transformative AI systems are developed safely

Preferred qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in policy communications, ideally at a high-growth technology company
  • Experience communicating about corporate governance, regulatory affairs, or oversight structures, and comfort explaining novel institutional arrangements to broad audiences
  • Existing relationships with security, governance, and tech policy reporters and influencers

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$265,000—$295,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. We manage various strategies across the capital structure, including privately negotiated senior debt; privately negotiated junior capital solutions in debt, preferred and equity formats; liquid credit including syndicated leveraged loans, collateralized loan obligations and high yield bonds; asset-based finance and real estate. The scale and breadth of our platform offers the flexibility to invest in companies large and small, through standard or customized solutions. At our core, we share a common thread of intellectual rigor and discipline that enables us to create value for our clients. HPS was established in 2007 as a unit of Highbridge Capital Management, LLC (“HCM”), a subsidiary of JPMorgan Asset Management (“JPMAM”). On March 31, 2016, the senior executives of HPS acquired HPS and its subsidiaries from JPMAM and HCM (the “Transaction”.[i] Following the Transaction, JPMAM retained a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently redeemed in April 2022. In June 2018, affiliates of Dyal Capital Partners made a passive minority investment in HPS. In February 2022, an affiliate of The Guardian Life Insurance Company of America made a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently increased in August 2024. On July 1, 2025, BlackRock acquired the business and assets of HPS, with 100% of consideration paid in BlackRock equity (the “HPS/BlackRock Transaction”). The HPS/BlackRock Transaction brings together BlackRock’s corporate and asset owner relationships with HPS’s diversified origination and capital flexibility. BlackRock and HPS have formed a new private financing solutions business unit (“PFS”) led by Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson, creating an integrated franchise with approximately $370 billion in client assets, including $205 billion of private credit assets.[ii] This combined platform, which has more than 590 investment professionals and approximately 1,300 employees globally,[iii] offers broad capabilities across senior and junior credit solutions, asset-based finance, real estate, CLOs and GP-LP solutions. As part of the HPS/BlackRock Transaction, Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson have joined BlackRock’s Global Executive Committee, and Scott Kapnick has been appointed as an observer to the BlackRock Board. This role works closely with fund accountants to ensure accurate and timely delivery of reporting requirements. Responsibilities Specific responsibilities will include but not be limited to the following: Support coordination and execution of the annual financial statement audits for US Credit Funds, consisting of ~100 separate financial statements Partner with Fund Accounting, Finance, Operations, Legal, Compliance, Tax, and business teams.
